Both turn on the mother's ignorance in the veri: அறியாமையின் வெறியென மயங்கி and அறிந்தனள் அல்லள் அன்னை. They count different harms: அன்னையும் அருந்துயர் உழந்தனள் ... எய்யாது விடுதலோ கொடிதே, against இம்மறை அலர் ஆகாமையோ அரிதே. Akananuru 98's sharper fear, of the hill man's hearing (கான்கெழு நாடன் கேட்பின்), goes unmentioned, but the teaches is true.

Verse 1 is the hunter's question, காணீரோ ஏமரை போந்தன ஈண்டு. Verse 9 names that kind of asking as a ruse, வஞ்சமே என்னும் வகைத்தால் ஓர் மாவினாய், and has the asker taken (நெஞ்சை நலங்கொண்டார்). Same poet and book, so the pretext and the confession form a real pair.

Bathing in the flood is the shared act: the rival's யாம் அஃது அயர்கம் சேறும் ... பெரும்புனல் வந்த இருந்துறை, and the wife's புதுப்புனல் ஆடக் கண்டோர் ... பலரே. The scandal/triumph contrast in teaches is true. Neither poem limits or conditions the other, so qualifies does not fit.

poems.note: The beasts' hunger ending is a seasonal state, not an act of a person of the situation.
Line 2 (மேற்றுச் சிறுதாய காய்வஞ்சி) is obscure; no native vehicle can be read with confidence.

iraicchi.act: the female monkey takes the kaanthal buds for wedding buds (மணமுகை) and celebrates
iraicchi.sense: a mock wedding on the hill while the millet guard has ended (புனமும் அடங்கின காப்பு) hints that the man should now bring the real marriage

poems.note: The clouds are both an open simile (போல) and the season sign the question turns on, so striking them removes the poem's sense.
The horses are the poem's subject and are joined to the speaker by an explicit என் நெஞ்சம் போல.

iraicchi.act: the dove climbs the bare ukaay branch, broods (நினைந்து) and moans in distress
iraicchi.sense: the lone pining dove on the road she took gives the bereft mother's grief at home

poems.note: The nursing buffalo is an epithet of the father's town; what it implies for the lovers cannot be said in one firm sentence.
The bees that have fed in many groves and now hum on her hair suggest the straying man, but the poem and its empty thurai state no straying.
A narrative span of a longer idyll; the elephant-trunk simile is open and the rain is the event narrated.
The storks feeding in a row against her lonely stay is a flock, not one thing or a pair.

iraicchi.act: the stork goes to see the white heron's dead young and cries helpless, grieving for another's loss
iraicchi.sense: the shore's compassion for another's grief stands for the grace (அருள்) the man shows by agreeing to marry

iraicchi.act: the male monkey shakes down ripe fruit and the female with her young eats what she catches below
iraicchi.sense: the monkey feeds his mate and young while the man has left his and does not think of them (உள்ளார், கொடியர்)

poems.note: The lines are hard to construe; no vehicle or carrier can be secured.
The thunder striking the kaanthal it takes for a snake invites a reading of misdirected harm, but no second correspondence can be named.

iraicchi.act: the cock sparrow plucks sugarcane flowers to make a nest for his mate near her laying
iraicchi.sense: the sparrow readies a home for his pregnant mate while the man sends only the bard's sweet words

poems.note: The cow dusted with kaanthal pollen that its calf does not know matches the girl changed by the man's leaf garment and the household that would notice; the roles are inverted, since the poem's mother fears rather than fails to know.
